title: Health Risks in Construction
whatItIs: Construction is high-risk for ill health, not just accidents. Dust, asbestos, noise, vibration, lifting and chemicals can all cause disease, often slowly.
keyFacts: Main health risks: back and joint injuries, vibration, dermatitis, hearing loss from noise, asbestos diseases.
Asbestos is the biggest occupational disease risk to construction workers. Silica dust comes next.
Work-related cancers often appear more than 10 years after exposure, and up to 40 or 50 years later.
Treat health like safety: Assess the risks, Control them, then Review the controls.

keyFacts.text: The law requires health surveillance for some workers, depending on exposure to things like noise, asbestos or silica.

keyFacts: Wash your hands and face before eating, drinking or smoking, and eat away from the work area.

visual.caption: The main causes of work-related ill health on site

a.label: Health surveillance
points: Ongoing checks for workers exposed to things that can harm them
Legally required for some exposures, e.g. noise, asbestos, silica
Finds early signs so the controls can be improved

b.label: Wellbeing check
points: Not required by law and not linked to your work

onTheTest.question: Why are health risks on site often ignored, compared with accidents?
options: The harm can take many years to show
Health law does not apply to construction
onTheTest.why: HSE: serious ill health can take many years to develop, so harmful exposures get dismissed next to the instant impact of accidents.

onTheTest.question: According to HSE, what is the biggest occupational disease risk to construction workers?
onTheTest.why: HSE: asbestos is the biggest occupational disease risk to construction workers; silica comes next.

traps: Health checks alone don't protect you: the first priority is to stop the exposure.
Feeling fine now proves nothing: dust and asbestos diseases can take decades to appear.
Substances on your hands can get into your mouth when you eat or smoke: wash first.
